   At line 66 the p20_single_gen2 draws 16 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm above
   the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate
   200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line
   did it 215 times; 3,440 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not
   follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not
   mixed. Source wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A6, B1, B2, B3, B4 and 35 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A6, B1, B2, B3, B4 and 35 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.

   line 64:  p20.dispense(buf_vol, dest_well)
   At line 64 the robot added buffer to well F1 in slot 3, which already held library 6. The
   addition was 27% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with
   it that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the
   well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun
   down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the
   wells are not what the protocol says they are.
   Affected: well F1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix well F1 in slot 3 after line 64: `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
